definitions.databaseProxy: analysis_task WAITING + PROCESSING sampled every 0.5s; not RocketMQ queue depth
definitions.outboxDrainRate: peak PENDING divided by elapsed time from peak sample to the final positive PENDING sample
definitions.rocketMqThroughput: mean of positive 5s-rate samples for broker messages_in/messages_out; broker delivery, not task completion

outboxImplementation.scheduler: Spring @Scheduled fixedDelay; the delay starts after the previous publishPending invocation completes
outboxImplementation.selection: status PENDING/FAILED/PUBLISHING, next_retry_at due, order by id, LIMIT batchSize
outboxImplementation.claim: conditional single-row update to PUBLISHING with recovery timeout
outboxImplementation.completion: conditional single-row update from PUBLISHING to SENT after SEND_OK
outboxImplementation.retry: on exception mark FAILED, increment retry_count, delay next attempt by 30s
outboxImplementation.transactionBoundary: publisher method has no @Transactional boundary; select, claim, send and mark operations are not one database transaction

conclusion.currentBottleneck: Outbox publisher supply is the first limiter with batch size 20; ready stays empty and c4 receives no more work than c2.
conclusion.candidateResult: Batch size 100 moves backlog from database Outbox into RocketMQ inflight/lag, but does not improve c2 end-to-end throughput.
conclusion.recoveredRetryEvidence: candidate-b100 run 1 logged one syncSend timeout (RemotingTooMuchRequestException: sendDefaultImpl call timeout); the 30s Outbox retry recovered and all 1000 tasks succeeded.
conclusion.productionDefaultRecommendation: Do not retain batch size 100 as the production default from this experiment.
conclusion.queueingLatencyLimitation: The 5.3.2 exporter exposes metric descriptors, but no queueing_latency or lag_latency samples were emitted for this PushConsumer in any formal run.

resumeSafe.caveat: single-machine local environment with deterministic 100ms HTTP AI Stub; native broker rate is not task-completion rate
